results.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo: In Goma, two rehabilitated centres to provide temporary care for children affected by armed conflict
results.description: Finding a safe environment, receiving appropriate support and, above all, reconnecting with childhood: this is the opportunity offered by two Transit and Orientation Centres, one for boys and the other for girls, which have been rehabilitated and modernised in Goma, North Kivu Province, with financial support from MONUSCO through its Child Protection Section. Implemented in partnership with the Bureau for Volunteerism in the Service of Children and Health (BVES), this project, funded to the tune of nearly US$50,000, aims to improve reception and care conditions for children affected by armed conflict who have become separated from their families, as well as other vulnerable children in need of assistance and protection. The rehabilitation works included strengthening reception facilities, improving accommodation conditions and upgrading water, hygiene and sanitation facilities. Care spaces were also enhanced to provide children with a safer, more dignified environment tailored to their needs. For Murabazi Namegabe, Director of BVES, the completion of the works represents much more than an improvement in infrastructure: it makes it possible to restore the conditions necessary to receive children. “The completion of the project and the finishing works at the two transit centres, one for boys and the other for girls, now gives us the opportunity to welcome children. We had children who had been relocated and placed with temporary foster families while waiting for the works to be completed,” he explains. Beyond accommodation, the centres are also intended to promote children's self-reliance and well-being through various activities. BVES plans, in particular, to rehabilitate vegetable gardens, provide spaces for growing crops and develop small-scale poultry and rabbit farming. These initiatives are designed to improve living conditions and contribute to dignified care for the children. Preventing diseases and promoting good hygiene practices The modernisation of the buildings also represents an important step forward for children's health. The former facilities, which were made of wooden planks, did not always provide optimal accommodation and hygiene conditions. Dr Desanges MBOROYA, who is responsible for health education for children, welcomes this transformation: “I am happy with this change. The former buildings were made of wooden planks, but the newly modernised permanent structures will help prevent children and young people from falling ill.” Awareness-raising will also play an important role in the support provided to the children. They will receive guidance on good hygiene practices and disease prevention, particularly in the context of the Ebola outbreak. “As soon as the young people arrive, we will begin teaching them good hygiene practices and ways to prevent diseases. We will explain what this disease is and how they can protect themselves against it,” she says. Protecting children and preventing their re-recruitment Against a backdrop of persistent insecurity in several territories of North Kivu, these centres address a critical need: providing an independent facility where children who have left armed groups can be temporarily accommodated, protected and prepared for their return to their families and communities. For Mathieu Ndgongo Koni, Head of MONUSCO's Child Protection Section, these facilities help fill a significant gap in the existing care system. “We need a centre where these children can be temporarily accommodated, receive psychological care and where family tracing efforts can be accelerated. Whenever time permits, we also offer them vocational training in small trades,” he emphasises. Without appropriate care and support, these children remain exposed to several risks, including being recruited again by armed groups, exploited or marginalised. Temporary accommodation in a secure environment, combined with psychosocial support, is therefore an essential step towards their sustainable reintegration. The two centres also provide services to children from surrounding communities, who can benefit from certain essential social services. According to project data, the two facilities are expected to directly accommodate approximately 420 children per year: 220 girls and 200 boys. Beyond improving infrastructure, this initiative directly contributes to several aspects of MONUSCO's mandate. It strengthens the protection of civilians by providing safe spaces for vulnerable children, supports disarmament, demobilisation and reintegration activities for children associated with armed forces and armed groups (Child DDR), and facilitates assistance to victims of grave violations within the framework of the Monitoring and Reporting Mechanism (MRM). Distributed by APO Group on behalf of Mission de l'Organisation des Nations unies en République démocratique du Congo (MONUSCO).
